21 July, 2023
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice Sambasiva Rao Naidu
 M.A.C.M.A. No.1652 Of 2012
Judgment :

Being aggrieved by the award passed by Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-Cum-IV Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District in O.P. No.463 of 2007, dated 28.11.2011, wherein the Tribunal passed an award granting a sum of Rs.24,000/- together with interest @ 7.5% per annum and fixing the liability against the owner of the vehicle which involved in the accident, the appellant herein filed this petition under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as 'the Act').

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal-Cum-IV Additional District Judge, Ranga Reddy District
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. As could be seen from the impugned order and as per the grounds urged by the appellant, it seems that the appellant herein filed O.P. No.463 of 2007 before the above said Tribunal under Section 166 of the Act and sought for compensation of Rs.1,00,000/- on account of injuries caused to her in a motor vehicle accident that took place on 07.11.2005.

The appellant has claimed that on the above said date while she was proceeding to her house on a water tanker on which she was working, there was an accident when the driver of one D.C.M. Van bearing No.A.P.11.V.1254 which came in opposite direction, dashed the water tanker.

The appellant, who suffered grievous injuries in the accident, filed the said petition against the owner of the vehicle and also Insurance Company from which an insurance policy was obtained by its owner.

The Tribunal having recorded the evidence of both parties and considering the oral and documentary evidence allowed the petition in part and granted a sum of Rs.24,000/- towards compensation under various heads and fixed liability against the owner of the vehicle only and dismissed the petition against the 2nd respondent/ Insurance Company.
3. The appellant has filed this petition contending that the order of the Tribunal is opposed to the very spirit and object of the provisions of the Act.
The Tribunal committed a grave error by not taking into consideration the oral and documentary evidence and awarded meager amount of compensation.
She has also claimed that the Tribunal committed an error by dismissing the petition against the 2nd respondent without assigning any valid and convincing reasons.

She has disputed the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal and sought for set aside the award and also sought for enhancement of the compensation and to make the other respondents liable to pay the compensation amount.

4. Heard both parties.
5.

Now the following point arose for consideration:

sentences.text: " Whether the claim of appellant for enhancement of the compensation can be considered on the basis of oral and documentary evidence adduced before the Tribunal and whether the 2nd respondent/Insurance Company can be made liable to pay the compensation as sought for"?
POINT 6.

As could be seen from the amount awarded, it is very clear that soon after the above referred accident, a complaint was lodged with the police, who concluded the investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of the D.C.M. Van.
The appellant who was examined as P.W.1, exhibited certified copies of FIR, charge sheet, scene of offence panchanama, medical report and bills in support of her claim.
The 2nd respondent i.e. Insurance Company has examined R.W.1 and marked copy of insurance police as Ex.B.1, the driving license of driver of DCM Van as Ex.B.2.
There is no dispute about the accident and the involvement of the D.C.M. van in the accident.
However, the 2nd respondent has claimed that the vehicle is a goods vehicle and the driver, who was on wheel at the time of accident had no driving license to drive such a transport vehicle.

In support of said claim,
reliance was placed on Exs.B.1 and Ex.B.2.
The other contention on which the present petition filed is with regard to less amount of compensation awarded by Tribunal below.

In the above impugned order, it was observed that the appellant is entitled to a sum of Rs.2,000/- towards transport expenditure, a sum of Rs.5,000/- was awarded towards medicines and extra-nourishment and a sum of Rs.5,000/- was also awarded under the head of pain and suffering apart from a sum of Rs.12,000/- towards loss of earnings.
7.

The Tribunal observed that in the said accident the appellant might have used some transport facility for which she could have spent Rs.2,000/- since there is sufficient proof to believe that the appellant spent some more amounts for medicines.
Taking into consideration of the injuries, the Court below rightly awarded an amount of Rs.5,000/- towards medicines and nourishment
in addition to the above another amount of Rs.5,000/- was awarded under the head of pain and suffering.
The appellant did not produce any proof of her employment or salary.

According to her oral evidence, she was a coolie and getting a sum of Rs.5,000/- per month and at the time of her evidence she has admitted before the Court below that she was getting a sum of Rs.2,000/- per month as wages from the employer.
In fact, no such employer was examined.
In spite of this, the Court below considered the request of the appellant and granted a sum of Rs.12,000/- as loss of earnings for four months @ Rs.3,000/- per month.

In fact the appellant herself admitted before the Court that she was receiving Rs.2,000/- per month and there was no sufficient proof that she suffered for four months and she has not attended to her duties.
However, the Court below did not grant any sum towards the grievous injuries.

Taking into the above stated circumstances into consideration a substantial amount of Rs.12,000/- was awarded which in the opinion of this Court is sufficient to be treated as it is for the injuries and also towards the loss of earnings.
Therefore, the Tribunal rightly awarded an amount of Rs.24,000/- and the appellant could not be placed any other material for enhancement of the said amount.
8. The next aspect that was raised by the appellant in the present appeal is about the liability of the 2nd respondent.

The petition against the 2nd respondent was dismissed by the Tribunal below on Smt. Goda Rajamani , Rajamma vs P.Ravinder And Another on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87867028/

sentences.text: 2 the ground that the driver of the vehicle was not having license to drive transport vehicle, cannot be engaged to drive D.C.M. Van thereby the Court below exonerated the Insurance Company from its liability.
In fact, it is settled position of law that when there is no dispute that the driver of a vehicle is having a license to drive the light motor vehicle he can drive a transport vehicle.

As per the evidence placed by the appellant, the vehicle involved in the accident is not a heavy motorcycle, it is only a D.C.M. Van and the respondent did not produce any evidence to show that the same was used for transport purpose.
However, since the driver was having a valid license to drive light motorcycle he can be permitted to drive the DCM Van and on that the 2nd respondent/ Insurance Company cannot escape its liability.

But the Court below on a wrong presumption dismissed the petition against the 2nd respondent, thereby the award can be set aside to that extent and the 2nd respondent can be made to pay the compensation fixed by the Tribunal below.
9.
In the result, the appeal is allowed in part with the above modification.

Both the respondents are liable to pay the compensation awarded by the Tribunal with costs and interest at the rate of 7.5%
per annum from the date of petition.
As a sequel, pending Miscellaneous Applications, if any, shall stand closed.

__ JUSTICE SAMBASIVA RAO NAIDU Date:
21.07.2023.
